observation_summary: The BrentSolver throws an IllegalArgumentException when one of the function endpoints is zero, even though a zero value at an endpoint indicates that the root has been found.
reasoning_summary: The root cause is a missing check for zero values at the function endpoints. The current implementation only checks if the product of the endpoint values is non-negative (sign >= 0), which incorrectly flags cases where one of the endpoints is exactly zero as invalid. Adding a check to return the root if either endpoint value is zero corrects the logic.
evidence_used: Bug report description: 'The exception should not be thrown with values [0.0,-101945.04630982173] because 0.0 is positive.'
Bug report description: 'One way to fix it would be to add this code after the assignment of yMin and yMax: if (yMin ==0 || yMax == 0) { return 0; }'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the algorithm is failing to find the root, the specific mechanism of failure is the lack of a guard condition to handle the zero-value edge case, which is a classic 'Checking' defect.
